ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The mandatory protocol requires each shareholder, director, authorised signatory and beneficial owner to be screened continuously against (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) UK HM Treasury consolidated list, (iv) EU sanctions list, and (v) the Hong Kong SAR and PRC domestic sanctions and AML lists. Individual UBOs are subject to PEPs identification using risk-based triggers, including current and former prominent public functions, family and close associates, and negative adverse-media verification. All screening must be recorded with time-stamped evidence, and automatic rescreening in no more than 30 days is required following any sanctions list update. For this low-risk matcha trade, enhanced due diligence is still required on non-resident holding entities and source-of-funds documentation for matcha procurement. Good standing verification against the Hong Kong Companies Registry and mainland SAMR systems is also required before filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry (ICRIS) online name search and name reservation for new companies; mainland PRC counterpart is the SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration System for the China shareholder or branch side
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), a Hong Kong company may adopt an English name, a traditional Chinese name, or both. The Chinese name must use traditional Chinese characters only, and any English transliteration must be phonetically or semantically acceptable to the Registrar. The four-tier naming hierarchy comprises (1) prohibited words, (2) names requiring consent from a competent authority, (3) names identical or too similar to an existing registered company, and (4) distinctive names that pass the statutory test. The Registrar will reject names that are scandalous, offensive, imply a Crown or Government connection, or that are likely to mislead the public as to the nature of the business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 21 days of a name rejection, the applicant may use ICRIS to file a re-application with a distinct name or submit a written appeal to the Registrar of Companies under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). The appeal must state the grounds in full and include evidence of consent from any conflicting existing company, a statutory declaration of distinctiveness, or proof that the proposed name is not in a prohibited category. If the Registrar denies the appeal, the applicant may name the Registrar as respondent and apply to the Court of First Instance for judicial review or an amendment order within 28 days. Each re-filing attracts an administrative fee. Counsel should first attempt to resolve the conflict by adjusting the proposed name or by obtaining a letter of no-objection from the prior registrant before seeking judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as a statutory registered office for a Hong Kong company because the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) requires a physical address in Hong Kong for service of documents. For the mainland PRC side, SAMR likewise requires a legal operational address; a postal or mailbox address will be rejected by tax authorities and banks. For the matcha distribution business, the Inland Revenue Department and licensed banks require a genuinely staffed physical office or storage facility reflecting active commercial substance. A virtual office may be used only for marketing correspondence, but the registered office, bank account KYC, and tax returns should all use a physical leased premises with adequate records and personnel.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspections by the Inland Revenue Department, Companies Registry, or mainland SAMR/tax authorities are possible. For a low-risk organic matcha powder trading entity, the quantified risk is low-to-medium, approximately 15% per annual regulatory cycle. Inspection checklist: 1) verify that the registered office is a physical leased space named on the lease; 2) ensure the company secretary and at least one local director or employee can attend; 3) maintain books, invoices, import/export records, bills of lading, matching certificates, source of funds, and UBO screening files; 4) ensure business licenses are posted; 5) confirm bank records correspond to trade flows; and 6) have legalization and apostille documents ready for verification. Failure to satisfy physical inspection may result in strike-off, tax reclassification, or suspension of banking facilities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) of the Laws of Hong Kong, particularly Sections 67 (Company Name), 68 (Reservation of Company Name), 100 (Power to Make Application for Incorporation), 101 (Incorporation by Registration), 103 (Effect of Incorporation), 109 (Register of Members), 112 (Statement of Capital and Initial Shareholding), 113 (Return of Allotment), 120 (Registered Office), 121 (Change of Registered Office), 153 (Appointment of Directors), 157 (Appointment of Company Secretary), 158 (Qualifications of Company Secretary), 405 (Annual Return), and 474 (Principal Officer's Obligations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Registry of Companies, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, 14/F, United Centre, 95 Queensway, Admiralty, Hong Kong
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Form NNC1 (Application for Incorporation and Statement of Capital and Initial Shareholding) filed with the Companies Registry, together with Articles of Association and the specified Incorporation Fee
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622); a standard practice of issuing one or more shares with a par value of HKD 1.00 per share is adopted solely to evidence the members' limited liability and the statement of capital. All subscribed share capital shall be credited as fully paid and may remain unblocked; no escrow, impoundment, or blocked capital account is required by the Companies Registry or the Hong Kong Monetary Authority for the formation or continued validity of the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as a formal resolution of the sole director and all the incorporators of the company, duly convened as the first meeting of the board of directors on the date of incorporation, that: (1) The incorporation of the company and its registration under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) be and hereby is ratified, confirmed, and approved, together with the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association adopted at the time of incorporation. (2) The share capital structure of the company be confirmed as set forth in the initial statement of capital filed with the Companies Registry; the subscribers' allotments be approved; and the issue of shares be recorded in the register of members, with share certificates issued under the common seal or under the signatures of two authorized officers as required by law. (3) The registered office of the company, as notified to the Companies Registry, be adopted and maintained as the official registered office of the company under Section 120 of the Companies Ordinance; the director and the company secretary be empowered to file changes of registered office and to receive all statutory notices, process, and communications on behalf of the company. (4) The directors be and hereby are authorized, jointly and severally, to open and operate bank accounts with such licensed banks or authorized financial institutions in Hong Kong or abroad as they shall select, to designate authorized signatories, to establish account mandates, and to execute all account-opening forms, signature cards, resolutions, letters, and instruments necessary to give effect to such arrangements, provided that any payment instruction in excess of USD 50,000 be signed by two designated directors or the director together with the company secretary. (5) The Director be appointed and appointed as the first director of the company, and the Company Secretary be appointed as company secretary in accordance with Section 157 of the Companies Ordinance, each such appointment to take effect immediately and to continue until resignation, removal, or vacation of office in accordance with the Articles of Association. (6) The Director and the Company Secretary, or either of them, be authorized and directed to prepare, execute, and deliver all statutory returns, applications, declarations, and instruments of every kind, and to do all acts and things as may be necessary or expedient to implement the foregoing resolutions and to carry on the business of the company, including the appointment of auditors, the establishment of accounting records, the adoption of bank mandates, and the execution of commercial agreements for the cross-border procurement, sale, distribution, and trading of organic culinary and ceremonial grade matcha powder under ISIC 4631, and to cause the company to comply with all applicable corporate governance, taxation, accounting, anti-money laundering, and reporting obligations under the laws of Hong Kong and any other relevant jurisdiction. THIS RESOLUTION IS FINAL, BINDING, AND EFFECTIVE AS OF THE DATE OF INCORPORATION.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry (e-Name Search and Online Name Reservation System, Hong Kong SAR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an exact and phonetically similar name search against the Companies Registry's database to ensure the proposed English and Chinese names do not conflict with existing registered names, reserved names, trademarks, or prohibited statutory names. Submit Form NNC1 together with the online name reservation request or, if the name has not been reserved, pay the applicable name reservation fee. The name must comply with Section 67 and Section 68 of the Companies Ordinance, and shall contain the term 'Limited' or the Chinese equivalent as a suffix. Include in the submission the proposed principal business address, the proposed liability of members being limited by shares, and the intended business scope referencing ISIC 4631 for wholesale trading of matcha powder. After approval, retain the name reservation reference to be used in the incorporation filing. Should the name be refused, select an alternative name or apply to the Companies Registry for a change of name, in each case within five business days, and resubmit the Form NNC1 with the revised name.
required_dossiers: Completed Form NNC1 (Application for Incorporation and Statement of Capital and Initial Shareholding)
Proposed Articles of Association (Articles) duly signed by all subscribers
Proposed English name or Chinese translation of the company name
Identity cards or passports of each subscriber, director, and company secretary
Proof of residential or correspondence address for each promoter or director
Name reservation confirmation or name search reference (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a query, refusal, or suspension due to unacceptable name, incomplete signatures, or defective Articles, the applicant shall, within 3 business days, submit a formal written explanation, corrected Form NNC1, and amended Articles, or file a fresh application under a new reserved name. If the registry suspects a prohibited name or unauthorized 'Limited' usage, the applicant may request an administrative review by the Registry's Name Review Committee or make a new application without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (Online e-Registry Portal and Counter Services at Admiralty)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the name reservation, file the incorporation package via the Companies Registry's e-Registry service or in person at the Companies Registry. The package consists of Form NNC1, signed Articles of Association, and the incorporation fee to the government. The Form NNC1 must state the initial capital structure, the number of shares, the class of shares, the par value, and the full names and addresses of at least one director and one company secretary. Verify that the proposed director is a natural person of at least 18 years of age and that the company secretary satisfies the requirements of Section 158, or that the sole director and sole subscriber are the same person where permitted. Ensure each subscriber signs the Articles with the statutory statement of compliance confirming no contravention of the Companies Ordinance is committed. If the Registrar is satisfied, the Certificate of Incorporation will be issued with a company number and incorporation date.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form NNC1
Signed Articles of Association (English or Chinese or bilingual)
Consent to act as director or secretary (required where applicable)
Proof of identity and address of director(s) and shareholder(s)
Statement of compliance or consent by each subscriber that all requirements of the Companies Ordinance have been complied with
Prescribed government fees (HKD 1,720 as at filing date or current gazetted fee)
Business address of the registered office in Hong Kong (must be a physical address, not a P.O. Box)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended due to missing or conflicting information, the applicant shall respond in writing within 3 business days by filing Form NNC1 supplement or a letter of clarification with corrected particulars, and resubmit original signed documents if notarized or authenticated copies are rejected. If the Registrar refuses registration, the applicant may apply for judicial review within the applicable statutory limitation period, or re-submit a clean incorporation package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office, Statutory Records, and Officers Appointment Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department (Business Registration Office), Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, ensure that the registered office address is a physical premises in Hong Kong and that official notice of the registered office (Form NR1) is filed with the Companies Registry if the address differs from the initial filing. Prepare and keep at the registered office the statutory records: register of members, register of directors and secretaries, minutes of directors' meetings, accounting records, and share certificates. File the Notice of Particulars of Directors and Secretaries (Form ND2A) and the Notice of Change of Registered Office (NR1) if required. Concurrently, apply to the Inland Revenue Department for the Business Registration Certificate (Form IRBR1) within one month of incorporation and display the certificate at the registered office. Obtain the Company's First Set of Statutory Records and issue share certificates to subscribers. Ensure the company secretary is appointed, and if the secretary is a natural person, the person must be resident in Hong Kong or, if a corporate secretary, have its registered office or place of business in Hong Kong.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation dated from Companies Registry
Form NR1 (Notice of Registration of Registered Office) where applicable
Form ND2A (Notice of Particulars of Director and Secretary)
Register of members, register of directors, and register of company secretaries
Business Registration Application (Form IRBR1) with the Business Registration fee to the Inland Revenue Department
Share certificates and minute book
Consent forms from directors and secretary
Statement of capital already filed in Form NNC1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry or Business Registration Office queries the physical address, officer eligibility, or consent to act, the company shall rectify within 3 business days by filing Form NR1 or ND2A with corrected particulars, or by appointing a qualified alternate director/secretary and filing the corresponding notice, with the original consent forms to be produced upon request. If registration of business is delayed, pay the late fee and apply for a reversal or appeal to the Business Registration Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Banking Authorization, and Anti-Money Laundering Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Banks or Authorized Financial Institutions under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155), Hong Kong Monetary Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approach the selected licensed bank in Hong Kong to open a corporate account under the authority granted by the first Board resolution. Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, Articles of Association, the Board resolution authorizing account opening, director identifications, and proof of address. Provide the bank with a description of the company's trading business, including cross-border procurement and wholesale distribution of organic culinary and ceremonial grade matcha powder, complete with the anticipated counterparty jurisdictions (especially China and Hong Kong), expected annual volume, and the intended payment rails of Swift TT and wire transfer. The bank will conduct customer due diligence and AML risk assessment; because the business is classified as Low_Risk_Standard, the bank may request invoices, purchase contracts, and details of the supply chain. After account opening, set up dual authorization for wire transfers above a threshold as specified in the Board Resolution. Review the standard terms for fees, foreign exchange spreads, and compliance obligations before executing the account mandate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Business Registration Certificate
Certificate of Incumbency or register of directors (current within 30 days)
Certified copies of Articles of Association
Board Resolution authorizing the opening of bank accounts and designated signatories
Passport or Hong Kong identity card of each director, shareholder, and authorized signatory
Proof of residential address of each signatory (e.g., utility or bank statement within 3 months)
Organizational structure and ultimate beneficial ownership declaration
Business profile, pro-forma invoices or contracts relating to matcha powder trade
AML questionnaire and declaration of source of funds
Notice of appointment of company secretary and registered office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further information or places the account opening on hold, the company shall promptly provide the complete UBO chart, source-of-funds evidence, trade invoices, and corporate chart. If the bank formally declines, the company may apply to a second licensed bank; no restriction applies to multiple concurrent banking relationships. If the bank files a suspicious transaction report, the company should remedy by ensuring transparent documentation of the matcha powder trade and update its internal compliance policy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Filings, Tax Registration, and Business Licence Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Companies Registry, Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of incorporation, ensure the Business Registration Certificate is obtained and displayed. Submit the Notice of Particulars of Director and Secretary (ND2A) and maintain the registered office. File any annual return under Section 405 within 42 days after the anniversary of the incorporation date, unless the company is a dormant company exempted by the Companies Ordinance. If the matcha powder trading activities will generate profits in Hong Kong or from Hong Kong sourced business, register with the Inland Revenue Department for Profits Tax; if the business is fully offshore, document the claim and maintain supporting evidence of the place of contract, negotiation, and performance. Although a food trading business that is purely wholesale distribution generally does not require a specific business license for import/export of matcha powder under Hong Kong's organic food regime, verify with the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department whether any food premises registration is required for the physical warehousing stage. For purity claims labelled 'organic,' ensure that any product labels comply with the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (Cap. 362) and the Chinese organic certification standards applicable in the People's Republic of China, and obtain any required proof of organic certification from the country of origin.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate
Certificate of Incorporation
Form ND2A and NR1 as filed
Annual return (Form NAR1) when due
Profits Tax return (Form IRB1) when issued
Rent, lease, or title deed of registered office address
Supply chain documents supporting offshore income claim, if applicable
Organic certificates and product specification sheets for matcha powder
Trade Descriptions compliance documents and labels
Customs import/export declarations where cross-border shipments occur
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD issues a penalty for late business registration or late annual return, the company may apply to the IRD for remission or reduction of penalties based on reasonable excuse and prompt rectification, and file a notice of objection within the statutory timeframe. If the Companies Registry imposes a penalty for late filing of annual return, apply to the Registry for a reduction and file the return immediately. For trade description issues, withdraw or relabel non-compliant products and coordinate with the affected enforcement authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department (for import/export licensing), Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (for food safety related registration), and Trade and Industry Department (for import/export licence requirements under the Import and Export (Strategic Commodities) Regulation; none is required for ordinary foodstuffs unless regulated substances are involved)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Registration / Import-Export Licence is Not Applicable to pure wholesale distribution of matcha powder under Hong Kong law; however, if the company maintains a physical storage or warehousing facility in Hong Kong, it must obtain a Food Storage Permit or designated food business registration from the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department under the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X) and maintain compliance with the Dangerous Goods Ordinance (Cap. 295) if any aerosol or chemical additives are stored.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD), Hong Kong SAR
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration / Exempt for trade and wholesale distribution activities; absent the construction of any industrial building, chemical processing, or storage of hazardous substances in quantities exceeding the scheduled thresholds, the proposed matcha powder distribution activity does not trigger a designated EIA project under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499) or a statutory EIA Report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to a pure trading and distribution activity in Hong Kong because there is no manufacturing discharge, no industrial wastewater generation, and no volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from production processes. In the event of a limited packaging repacking operation on a leased site, all oily aerosols, dust extraction, and floor washings must comply with the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 311) and the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354) standards, including PM10 emissions below 1.0 mg/m³ and peak odour concentration of not more than 5 O.U. (odour units), and the company shall hold a Waste Disposal Licence if annual hazardous waste production exceeds 5 tonnes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Fire Services (Fire Hazard) Regulation (Cap. 45) is mandatory if the company leases an industrial warehouse; the premises must be inspected by the Fire Services Department, with exit pathways and fire-fighting equipment certified before use. The structural load and occupation of any warehouse must be approved by the Buildings Department under the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), including submission of Form FSI/FSIS/1+2 for fire service installations where applicable. The company shall also obtain a Certificate of Compliance from the Labour Department by implementing the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) workplace safety measures, including risk assessments for handling heavy matcha powder sacks, dust suppression, and emergency evacuation plans prior to operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China and the local competent tax office at the registered address of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture; electronic registration, filing and invoice administration are completed through the STA Unified Electronic Tax Bureau portal and the Golden Tax Phase IV invoice system. For any Hong Kong SAR element, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of Hong Kong and its Business Registration Office are the competent authorities for Hong Kong business registration and Hong Kong-sourced profits taxation, but the PRC-resident JV's primary statutory tax registration is with the STA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: incorporate the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the legal taxpayer identification number for PRC tax purposes. Step 2: complete tax registration with the competent local STA office within 30 days after issuance of the business license, filing the JV capital structure, legal representative, business scope, bank accounts, accounting system and shareholder information. Step 3: determine VAT taxpayer status by electing general VAT taxpayer treatment or small-scale taxpayer treatment where lawful, and register for VAT invoice issuance through the electronic tax bureau. Step 4: complete export tax rebate registration with the STA export rebate system, including customs export registration, foreign-exchange settlement bank details and the designated export rebate bank account. Step 5: for a foreign non-resident shareholder, no separate Chinese TIN is generally required unless it has a taxable permanent establishment or derives China-source income subject to withholding; any required non-resident tax identity is procured through the non-resident taxpayer registration/identity application in the STA electronic portal. For any Hong Kong entity, the IRD Business Registration Certificate and taxpayer file number are obtained under the Business Registration Ordinance, unless no Hong Kong business or Hong Kong-sourced profit exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is a PRC resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income under the PRC Corporate Income Tax Law; there is no pass-through eligibility, no territorial-scope election, and no general tax-exempt zone status for this wholesale trading entity).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification (the PRC does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election regime; entity-level taxation is mandatory). Administrative elections that remain available include election of small-scale versus general VAT taxpayer status, election of special tax treatment for qualified corporate restructuring transactions under STA notices, and revenue-recognition/accounting elections only where expressly permitted by PRC tax law. For a Hong Kong shareholder or related Hong Kong vehicle, a territorial-source profits tax claim may be available before the IRD, but this does not alter the PRC JV's entity-level tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China under the PRC VAT regime and VAT Law framework; the Hong Kong SAR does not impose VAT, GST or general sales tax, so the indirect tax regime for this cross-border matcha powder trade is exclusively PRC VAT with export zero-rating and export rebate mechanics.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 (VAT-exclusive turnover) from wholesale supplies of goods triggers mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration for the JV; below this threshold the JV may remain a small-scale taxpayer under the simplified collection method. All newly established PRC entities must complete tax registration within 30 days of business license issuance, and export rebate registration is separately required before claiming export zero-rating.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-approved electronic invoicing and tax-control infrastructure, either via full-digital electronic invoices or through National Tax Control equipment under Golden Tax Phase IV. Every VAT special invoice carries an anti-counterfeit invoice code, tax-control cipher, and verification mechanism, and invoice data is transmitted electronically to the STA in near real-time; buyers must verify invoices through the national electronic invoice verification system, and no off-platform statutory VAT special invoice may be issued for input credit or export rebate purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of organic culinary and ceremonial grade matcha powder from PRC customs territory qualifies for the 0% VAT export rate and corresponding export rebate (exemption and refund) treatment, provided the JV is a VAT general taxpayer, the goods are physically exported from the PRC, the export customs declaration and transport documents are authentic and consistent, and export proceeds are collected and repatriated in accordance with foreign-exchange control rules. The zero-rating applies to the export sale; input VAT on domestic procurement of the matcha powder inventory is refundable through the export rebate system only after documentary matching with customs, invoicing and banking records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export goods declaration/customs bill of entry) showing the matcha powder HS classification, declared customs value, destination country and customs release data
Bill of Lading, multimodal transport document or airway bill evidencing physical carriage of the goods from PRC customs territory to the overseas buyer
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the customs declaration quantity, unit price and total invoice value
Export sales contract or purchase order with the overseas buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank export foreign-exchange settlement/collection statement confirming receipt of export proceeds from outside the PRC
Input VAT special invoice(s) (VAT Fapiao) for the domestic procurement of the matcha powder inventory, required for VAT export rebate computation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, customs administration and banking monitoring systems cross-match export declarations, VAT invoices, transport data and export proceeds. If export zero-rating is claimed on false, unverified or non-repatriated documentation, the claimed refund or zero-rated benefit is clawed back with statutory late-payment interest; under Article 63 of the PRC Tax Administration Law, a fine from 50% to 5 times the evaded tax may be imposed. False customs declarations are separately penalized under the PRC Customs Law, and fraudulent export VAT rebate claims may constitute criminal fraud under the PRC Criminal Law, giving rise to imprisonment and fines. Failure to receive export proceeds within the 180-day repatriation deadline generally converts the zero-rated/refunded position into a taxable and clawed-back obligation unless an STA-recognized exceptional circumstance is properly documented and approved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and its State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for the Mainland China component; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for the Hong Kong SAR component.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The treasury mandate spans two distinct legal environments. Hong Kong SAR maintains full currency convertibility and has no foreign exchange controls, capital account restrictions, or surrender requirements; HKD and CNY are freely deployable and the HKMA does not intervene in market-based clearing. In contrast, the Mainland Chinese component operates under SAFE's current account and capital account administration. Current account transactions (goods trade, services, remittances) are generally convertible, provided a full evidentiary trail (contracts, invoices, customs declarations, tax vouchers) is presented to a designated licensed bank. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment into a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, require separate approval or SAFE registration, and the outflow side—especially profit remittances to the non-resident partner—is restricted until the entity holds audited financial statements, has paid enterprise income tax, and obtains a tax clearance certificate. The JV must open a dedicated foreign exchange capital account, file FDI registration, and ensure that each cross-border capital movement has a genuine and verifiable commercial rationale. Profit remittance hurdles are heightened by the requirement to demonstrate the availability of distributable after-tax reserves and to present a board resolution clarifying dividend allocation. Practically, the RMB is not freely convertible outside the limited current account and permitted capital account channels; offshore CNY in Hong Kong can be traded through CNH markets, but the movement of funds between the onshore and offshore pools must be routed through RMB clearing banks with proper trade documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For Mainland China under SAFE regulations, all export proceeds from goods trade must be repatriated into a domestic foreign exchange settlement account within 90 days from the date of export customs declaration, unless SAFE has granted an extended deadline. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the enterprise may retain the foreign currency or voluntarily convert to RMB, subject to the bank's post-settlement authenticity review. For the Hong Kong leg, there is no statutory surrender requirement, and export proceeds may be held indefinitely in any currency, though an internal treasury policy should avoid triggering any unintended mainland income recognition or economic substance concerns.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account + Foreign Exchange Capital Account (Escrow)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (HSBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Global Premier Operational Account with HKMA licensed entity
Trade Finance and Duty Drawback Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for Mainland China clearance. Fintech EMI platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Revolut, Wise Business) cannot issue a local bank account for a mainland-incorporated JV unless the EMI holds a PRC payment institution license, which currently does not cover commercial bank-grade current accounts. Mainland regulators mandate direct supervision by PBOC/SAFE on all domestic RMB and foreign currency clearing, so a non-bank intermediary is restricted to e-commerce agency collection under a specific certificate, not cross-border corporate treasury. In Hong Kong, licensed virtual banks and EMIs can provide multi-currency wallets and MT103-like settlements, but they are not a substitute for a full-service corporate bank when the entity requires documentary credits, import/export financing, and SAFE-linked services. The optimal structure is a domestic bank for all onshore flows and an EMI only as a supplementary receivable collection tool in Hong Kong, with daily sweeping to the HSBC or BOCHK accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mainland China: The legal representative and the financial controller must physically appear at the bank branch for the opening of both the basic deposit account and the foreign exchange capital account; remote and consular proxy opening is not permitted under PBOC Account Management Rules. Hong Kong SAR: Physical presence is the norm, but the HKMA accepts a director appointment with a notarized power of attorney and a remote video KYC interview for low-risk trading companies; the bank may still require one founding director to attend in person. For this Matcha distribution JV, we strongly recommend all statutory signatories to complete in-branch verification at the HK bank to avoid a 20-banking-day conditional approval period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership concentration through two dynamic control layers (Mainland partner and Hong Kong corporate director)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a signed ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) declaration, a certified corporate structure chart from formation agents, certificates of incumbency for all intermediate entities, and a notarized copy of the JV contract showing each partner's ultimate family ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade description risk for organic matcha: US FDA/European organic equivalency and certification gaps
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit OFDC (China Organic Food Development Center), ECOCERT, and USDA NOP organic certification certificates, a detailed product specification and ingredient list, batch-level Certificate of Analysis, and original sales contracts matching the exact HS tariff units used in the import declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice valuation or trade financing duplication for high-value powder shipments routed through Hong Kong
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide original SWIFT MT103 evidence, matching customs Form E or export declarations, a duly signed sales contract, two independent valuations from certified appraisers on delivery terms, transport insurance policy, and a warehouse receipt confirming physical stock movement through an unaffiliated logistics operator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP/sanctions-screening red flags when the non-resident shareholder operates in multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver global PEP and adverse media screening reports from a recognized database (Dow Jones or Refinitiv), audited financial statements of the shareholder, source-of-wealth documentation for the subscribed capital, and a legal declaration undertaking to maintain all transactions within the approved trade flow of the entity bank network only.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign partner's capital injection must first obtain SAFE/FDI registration at the subject bank, then transfer via SWIFT MT103 with the BPM6 purpose code for 'Equity capital and investment fund shares' to the JV's foreign exchange capital account. On arrival, the bank performs post-registration verification against the foreign investment negative list, the JV's business license, and the executed JV contract. For the HK treasury arm, capital can be funneled via a discretionary investment holding account, but if the HK entity receives payment for the inbound equity, the wiring reference must state 'Registered Capital Contribution under JV Agreement' to avoid a reserve-only classification, and the China side must complete the SAFE FDIC registration form within 15 days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, use SWIFT MT103 for all low-risk, low-value payments such as packaging materials, organic certification fees, and logistics, using the ISIC 4631 documentation template. For large purchase orders for ceremonial-grade matcha, use a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) at sight or a usance LC of up to 90 days, issued by the HK bank and advised through an ICBC correspondent branch to the supplier's bank in Japan or China. Documentary collections (DP/DA) are suitable for medium-value existing counterparties where a dedicated relationship already exists, but for new cross-border suppliers always prefer a confirmed, irrevocable LC. All disbursements should be routed via CIPS for CNY-denominated payments and CHATS for HKD-denominated immediate settlement, ensuring each payment reference includes the matcha HS code and the underlying sales contract number.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY forward contracts (USD/CNY, HKD/CNY) with genuine underlying trade exposure and settlement through SAFE licensed domestic banks
Offshore CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed in Hong Kong for CNH exposure, but strictly prohibited for onshore-incorporated JVs
Cross-currency swaps between HKD, USD, and RMB for long-term capital matching the tenor of the underlying import/export contract, maximum 12 months for working capital
Plain vanilla FX options (calls/puts) on USD/CNH for the Hong Kong treasury arm to protect matcha procurement costs, subject to HKMA regulatory approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary date of incorporation of the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating late registration fee from HKD 870 (up to 3 months) to HKD 3,480 (over 9 months); continued default leads to prosecution and administrative strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date shown on the current certificate; late renewal accrues interest from the expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a statutory late fee of HKD 300 per month or part of a month, capped at HKD 2,000, and a maximum fine of HKD 5,000; persistent non-renewal triggers cancellation of the Business Registration Certificate and cessation of lawful trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month from the date of issue of the return, extended to 3 months for e-filing under the IRD's extension circular; actual due date printed on the return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties from HKD 1,200 to HKD 3,000, estimated assessment by assessor, and prosecution with fines up to HKD 10,000 plus a daily default penalty of HKD 1,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form IR56B) Annual Statement of Remuneration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after 31 March or within one month from the issue date of the return, whichever is later
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Maximum fine of HKD 10,000, plus an additional daily fine of HKD 1,000 for continuing failure; the IRD may also estimate remuneration for tax assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No Hong Kong turnover, asset or headcount-based exemption exists. Under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every company incorporated in Hong Kong (including a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture operating through a HK company) must appoint a certified public accountant (practising) as auditor and produce audited financial statements each financial year, unless the company is dormant and has validly passed the necessary resolution not to have an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: HKFRS (fully converged with IFRS as issued by the IASB); eligible private companies may elect HKFRS for Private Entities; Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) Part 9 accounting provisions apply.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not impose a separate annual UBO return. The company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) at the registered office, update it within 7 days of any change in significant controllers, and report any allotment or transfer of shares using the prescribed Companies Registry form (e.g., Form NSC1 for allotments; Form NSC2 for share transfers) within 30 days of such event. The annual return (NAR1) simultaneously confirms the register of members and issued share capital.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Company Secretaries
Share Transfer Register (Annex to Register of Members)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No tax holiday or patent box applies to a pure matcha powder distribution JV. The standard China resident corporate income tax rate is 25%; a qualifying Small Low-Profit Enterprise is taxed at 20% with reduced effective rates of 5% or 10% on assessable income within prevailing statutory thresholds; a certified High and New Technology Enterprise may use the 15% preferential rate, and eligible R&D expenses were subject to a 100% additional deduction under the 2023-2025 incentive window, although a trading business will rarely satisfy the controlling-originality or R&D ratio tests.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, A-Class) for the resident Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax electronic filing system; non-resident dividend withholding and treaty-reduced-rate claims are separately filed on Form F100000 and ancillary withholding schedules through the same e-Tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional returns are due by the 15th day after the end of each calendar quarter; the annual A100000 return and final tax settlement are due by 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end, and any tax balance must be settled by the same date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number, legal name of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, registered address, industry classification (ISIC 4631 / NAICS 424490), tax residence classification and authorized representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record the Chinese JV as a resident enterprise; do not tick non-resident status. Disclose the ultimate Hong Kong parent in the related-party schedule; whenever the Hong Kong shareholder intends to claim the 5% dividend treaty rate, attach the Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declarations before the dividend is distributed, otherwise the statutory 10% withholding rate must be applied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis, fiscal year-end, main business income from wholesale distribution of culinary and ceremonial grade organic matcha powder, and revenue recognition policies for cross-border procurement and resale.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue consistently with the shipping terms and goods control; if the JV functions as a low-risk distributor buying from the Hong Kong parent and reselling to mainland customers, the commercial return must be supported by a Resale Price or TNMM benchmark selected from Chinese comparable distributors. Understated gross margins invite automatic transfer pricing scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue, operating costs, gross profit, and cost breakdown related to purchases of organic matcha powder from related suppliers, third-party growers, and logistics providers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every cross-border intercompany purchase from the Hong Kong parent must be at arm's length and documented contemporaneously. The invoice price, customs value, and corporate income tax deduction must be consistent; a forced transfer pricing adjustment will increase taxable income and may trigger special tax-adjustment interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general and administrative expenses, freight and storage costs, finance costs, foreign exchange losses, bad debt provisions, entertainment expenses, and tax-disallowed expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to the Hong Kong parent is subject to thin-capitalization limits: non-financial enterprises are bound by a 2:1 debt-to-equity safe harbor, and only arm's length financing is deductible. Excessive interest will be disallowed and may be reclassified as a deemed dividend subject to non-resident dividend withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and gains, including interest income, dividends received, foreign exchange gains, asset disposals, prior-year adjustments, and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Chinese JV is taxed on its worldwide income. Dividends or interest received from non-resident subsidiaries or offshore cash pools are taxable in China unless an explicit treaty or domestic exemption applies; foreign income taxes paid may be credited only where original tax payment certificates and residency documents are attached through Schedule A108000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit, tax-adjustment additions, tax-adjustment deductions, taxable income after loss carryforward and incentives, applicable tax rate, foreign tax credits, prepayments, and final tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle the final tax payable on Schedule A100000 and reconcile the distributable profit with the withholding tax base declared for the Hong Kong shareholder. If no withholding return is filed on deemed dividends, the tax authority may collect the under-withheld tax from the JV as withholding agent and charge daily late-payment surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty of RMB 2,000 per un-filed return, increased to RMB 10,000 for serious cases under Article 62 of the Tax Collection Administration Law; late payment adds a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. False reporting or fraudulent under-declaration is punishable under Article 63 by recovery of the shortfall plus a fine of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded; where the evasion amount is large, typically at least RMB 50,000 and more than 10% of total tax payable, criminal liability attaches under Article 201 of the Criminal Law with imprisonment up to seven years for aggravated circumstances.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (PRC domestic statutory withholding tax on dividends paid to a non-resident shareholder; reduced to 5% under the Mainland and Hong Kong SAR Double Taxation Arrangement if the Hong Kong beneficial owner directly holds at least 25% of the JV's paid-up capital and satisfies the beneficial ownership and substance conditions).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the 5% reduced dividend withholding rate, the Hong Kong shareholder must provide the Chinese JV with: (1) a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Inland Revenue Department; (2) a beneficial ownership declaration form; (3) evidence that the Hong Kong shareholder is not a conduit and does not pass on the dividend to a third-jurisdiction resident; and (4) the completed e-Tax treaty-relief filing and non-resident withholding voucher. The Chinese withholding agent must withhold 10% if the documentation is incomplete, and the Hong Kong shareholder may apply for a refund of the excess through a special administrative review and tax-authority-approved treaty benefit claim.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 10% domestic PRC withholding tax, reduced to 7% under the Mainland/HK arrangement for arm's length interest passing the beneficial ownership test and genuine loan registry documentation. Royalties: 10% domestic PRC withholding tax, reduced to 7% under the arrangement for approved categories of royalties, but the intangible must actually be exploited in China and the royalty rate must be arm's length and supported by an economic valuation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB thresholds for related-party transaction documentation under PRC CIT rules: annual tangible-asset transfers exceeding RMB 200 million; annual intangible-asset transfers exceeding RMB 100 million; annual financial-asset transfers exceeding RMB 100 million; and other related-party transactions exceeding RMB 40 million. A Master File is mandatory when aggregate annual related-party turnover exceeds RMB 1 billion; contemporaneous Local File and special adjustment documents must accompany the annual filing when thresholds are met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Chinese JV must demonstrate real business presence, management, staff, warehouse capacity and distribution activity inside mainland China. The Hong Kong shareholder claiming treaty benefits must maintain substantive economic substance in Hong Kong, including active decision-making functions and core income-generating activities (CIGA), and cannot be a passive shell; although mainland China does not apply the Hong Kong-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), the general anti-avoidance rule in Article 47 of the CIT Law and the anti-abuse provisions of the Mainland/HK tax arrangement are used to deny treaty relief to shell companies and artificial arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion from Domestic Revenue Misdeclaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating matcha powder sales, inflating cost of goods sold through fictitious reinvoicing from a Hong Kong intermediary, omitting cross-border e-commerce revenue, or fabricating purchase orders to reduce Chinese taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law: the tax authority will order rectification, recover unpaid tax plus a daily 0.05% late-payment surcharge, and impose a fine of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded; serious cases are prosecuted under Article 201 of the Criminal Law, carrying criminal fines and imprisonment up to seven years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved false accounting and used the limited-liability vehicle to conceal profits may have the corporate veil pierced under Article 20(3) of the PRC Company Law and be jointly and severally liable for civil restitution to the company and unexhausted tax liabilities; the legal representative is also placed on the SAT serious-violation blacklist, which triggers an exit-control/travel ban from China until the tax is settled, while criminal imprisonment up to seven years may be imposed for aggravated fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent sells organic matcha powder to the JV at inflated prices, leaving the Chinese distributor with sub-normal profits, or the JV pays excessive management fees, royalties, or interest to the Hong Kong party without performing corresponding functions, assets, and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 41, 44, and 47 of the PRC CIT Law, together with SAT Public Notice 2016 No.42 and the Special Tax Adjustments Implementation Measures, authorize the tax authority to re-determine taxable income using the arm's length standard; the resulting underpayment is subject to special tax-adjustment interest at the benchmark lending rate plus two percentage points; failure to provide contemporaneous documentation can trigger penalties up to RMB 50,000 under Article 70 of the Tax Collection Administration Law, in addition to full recovery of the adjusted tax and late surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the transfer pricing scheme is used to divert JV profits into the Hong Kong shareholder and is coupled with informal benefit conversion, directors can be held personally liable for asset restitution under the corporate-veil-piercing rule; the legal representative may be blacklisted and travel-banned by the tax authority's joint punishment mechanism, and directors who knowingly execute circular sham transactions risk civil forfeiture and, where fraud is proven, criminal liability for tax-related offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Beneficial Ownership Abuse and Withholding Shortfall
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Hong Kong shell entity with no office, staff, or investment-decision functions as the nominal shareholder to receive dividends at the 5% treaty rate while the ultimate beneficial owner is in a third country, or distributing dividends from the Chinese JV without withholding the statutory 10% tax, or routing royalty payments through Hong Kong to strip income from China without beneficial economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Mainland/HK tax arrangement and the Article 47 general anti-avoidance rule of the PRC CIT Law operate to deny treaty benefits; the Chinese payer is ordered to withhold the statutory 10% dividend tax or 10% passive-income tax, recover daily late surcharges, and pay a penalty under Article 69 of the Tax Collection Administration Law of 50% to 500% of the unpaid withholding tax; the tax authority may also impose blacklisting under the serious-violation joint punishment framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly arrange a sham Hong Kong beneficial owner and dividend channel can have the corporate veil pierced, becoming personally liable for the under-withheld tax and restitution of corporate assets; the legal representative is blacklisted and prohibited from leaving China until liabilities are cleared; where the arrangement is used to conceal tax from onward transfer, criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the Criminal Law may result in imprisonment up to seven years.
